01

The three questions, answered

New features, even over several jobs?

Yes. Every follow-up is a job.continue on the project: 0.5 IMD, up to 6 steps, same payer (pawai.eth), and the worker starts from the project's delivered tree. Chain as many as you like; each one ships a new version under the same site name when it carries ipfs: true.

One coherent feature set per job. A job that blocks loses its whole 0.5 IMD, so independent features in separate jobs limit the blast radius.

Bigger jobs with fewer steps?

Yes, within the per-step render limit: the plane renders each step as objective + that step's text and refuses anything over 8,000 characters. One big step can take almost all of it. More steps do not buy more room per step, only more distinct instructions, and the 16 KiB body cap binds from about four full steps on.

Steps are free: a 6-step job costs the same 0.5 IMD as a 1-step job.

How do steps combine?

Three shapes: chain (each step after the previous), fan_out_join (parallel implement steps, then integrate-project), dag (explicit dependsOn per step). The plane adds its own nodes: a design_critic on every website, four auditors and a judge on every launch.

The trap found today: a bundle does not pass through a review-only step. Never put implement → review → implement in a chain; make the second implement step depend on the first directly.

How much space each setting carries

Three limits bind, in this order of bite: the rendered step (objective plus one step's text, 8,000 characters, refused per step as objective_too_large), the step text itself (3,000 characters observed on the site body's step 1), and the whole request body (16 KiB on the wire). A continuation does not need to repeat the original brief. The worker reads the delivered tree and project.md, so the whole budget goes to what changes. Exact texts the builder must reproduce belong in the objective once, never repeated per step, because every step is rendered with the full objective.

chainbuild → check → document; audit → adapt → revieweach step sees the previous result; simplest to brief; the plane's own templates use it (27 of the newest 100 jobs)one failed node blocks the rest and the fee; an implement step after a review-only step restarts from the base tree (the bug of issue #6)launch #2147's three steps, 35 min; site job B blocked at the merge
fan_out_joinseveral components or contracts in parallel (implement-component, implement-one-contract), then integrate-projectwall-clock parallel; separate seats cannot see each other's work, so interfaces must be fixed in the objectivethe join merges several bundles: conflicts fail the join; one of 100 recent jobs used a parallel shapeuntested by us
daganything where a step needs two earlier results, or a review must see a specific treeexplicit dependsOn per step, so the docs step can depend on the build directly and a review can sit on two implement stepsmore to specify; the same merge rule applies when a step names two bundle-producing dependenciesone shape:dag job seen on the plane; workflow-planner is a skill that proposes one

What the plane adds to your steps

  • Website jobs get a design_critic (premium, reviews against the brief) that depends on the build step and on any docs step. site-content-check is yours to ask for; hosting happens only when every node is accepted.
  • Launches get write_foundry_tests, manifest, four audit_specialist nodes, an audit_judge and the deploy; a blocking finding parks the launch undeployed.
  • Workflows require an adversarial-review step and one website step last; the evaluator rewrites your draft at the quote.
The dependency trap (Identity-md/worker#6). A node receives only the bundles of its direct dependencies. A review step accepts without a bundle, so an implement step that depends only on that review gets nothing and starts from the base tree. Two sibling implement bundles then conflict when a later node needs both. Rule for every brief from now on: an implement step depends on the previous implement step, reviews come after the last implement step or in parallel with it, and a docs step either runs inside the build step's objective or depends on the build directly in a dag.

07

What is not possible right now, measured

Plane and payer

  • No payer action resumes a blocked job; the fee is spent (resultGuaranteed: false). A continuation is the remedy.
  • A continuation is accepted only from the wallet that paid the parent (403 payer_not_owner).
  • A bundle does not pass through a review-only step (issue #6); until fixed, write the dependency yourself.
  • Steps: at most 6. Body: 16 KiB. Rendered step: 8,000 characters. contracts ≤ 4 in a job, 1–8 in a contracts-only launch.
  • Seats cannot host sites (member_sites_closed); a job's site is hosted by the plane only, and only when every node accepted.
  • The design critic on website jobs and the audit panel on launches cannot be switched off.

Sworn's own contracts

  • Ownerless: no setter, pause or upgrade. Panel sizes (5 / 3 chain, 11 / 7 panel) and the uint16 spec ids are constants.
  • The pool pays only for catalog chain claims of WhitelistCurator members; shared facts and community specs are always paid by the requester.
  • applySharedFact marks the caller only; the 32 wallets apply the list themselves.
  • A false oracle answer is a spent 0.5 IMD (reason 8); the same request can be made again later.

Decisions already taken

  • Only the swarm site, no own hosting, not even as a fallback (decision 39).
  • Nothing is announced before the hosted site passes site-check and a manual pass (owner, 10-18).
